newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs and pork bellies seen steady to lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs and pork bellies seen steady to lower.

text.p: CME hog futures were expected to open steady to 0.250 cent per lb lower while pork belly futures were seen steady to 0.400 cent lower, livestock analysts said.

Pressure was seen in hog futures from moderating weather and increased hog runs. Futures slipped to one-month lows on Friday on the weather outlook and early cash market indications Monday were $0.50 to $1.50 per cwt lower as hogs backed up by two weeks of wintry weather start coming to market, they said.
However, much of the expected cash hog price break is already in the market, some sources said.
Higher pork cutout prices and likely normal cash hog marketings by later in the week could limit pressure. Any increase in demand for pork products will also spark support, they added.
Belly futures were also expected to be depressed by increased hog marketings and projected larger slaughter after setting two-month lows Friday, they said.

However, short covering could develop ahead of Tuesday's CME weekly out-of-town and USDA monthly U.S. Cold Storage reports. The reports are expected to show light belly storage numbers under year- ago levels, they said.

Analysts' estimates on the monthly USDA report pointed to total U.S. frozen belly stocks at between 37.4 million and 41.5 million lbs. This compares with 30.9 million on hand December 1 and 47.6 million in storage January 1, 1996.
Futures close early at 1200 CST/1800 GMT in observance of the Martin Luther King Jr holiday.
